text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

As part of a move designed to build a "third arm" in the gambling and entertainment industry, Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd will pay A$342 million to take out Showboat Inc's management contract at Sydney Harbour Casino and to take a 10 percent stake in the casino company. PBL has the potential to double its stake by 1999 and there are suggestions of a possible merger of Sydney Casino with Melbourne's Crown Casino. Page 1.

Count Financial Group yesterday launched a standard 7.45 percent mortgage through its national network of 370 accountancy firms, to be managed and funded by BankWest. The move signals a growing trend towards "one-stop shops" where clients can access home loans, insurance, superannuation and managed funds from the one source. Page 2.

In a second submission to the Federal Government's Wallis inquiry into the financial system, The Australian Business Chamber called for appropriate government support to implement a stock exchange second board to help small firms raise capital. With Australia's original second board abandoned in 1991, the chamber said a new second board could work, given the changes in technology. Page 3.

Highlands Gold Ltd last night continued to reject Placer Dome Inc's A$423 million takeover bid, claiming that although Highlands' A$160 million underwriting was unsuccessful, a restructuring of the PNG-based company was in the best interests of all shareholders. Page 15.

According to The Financial Times, the AMP Society intends to use its base in Britain to expand in Europe, ahead of the United States and Asia. AMP already owns Pearl Assurance and London Life in Britain and is looking to buy a "sizeable" British life and pensions company, the newspaper reported. Page 15.

At least six giant U.S. railroad companies have expressed an interest in the loss-making operations of the government-owned Australian National and National Rail. Recently purchasing privatised rail assets in the UK and Latin America, companies including Rail-Tex Inc, Burlington/Santa Fe, Kansas City Southern Industries, Western Rail and CSX, have requested more information to assess if they will launch bids. Page 15.
THE AUSTRALIAN

After the Packer family's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd announced it had struck a deal with United States-based Showboat to buy its 85 percent stake in the management company of Sydney Harbour Casino for A$240 million, and purchase a further 10 percent at A$1.85 a share, shares in the casino rocketed to a record high of A$2.27 yesterday. Page 19.

In a supplementary submission to the Wallis inquiry into the financial system, the Australian Bankers Association strongly rejected proposals to introduce deposit-protection insurance, warning bank customers will face increased fees if the insurance is introduced. The association's stance puts it at odds with the Reserve Bank of Australia, which supports the plan. Page 19.

After yesterday unveiling a 30 percent rise in revenue for the year to a record A$72.3 million, due largely to a strong real estate division, Sotheby's Australia managing director Justin Miller said the auction house expects to crack the A$1 million profit mark when it releases its 1996 results in March. Page 19.

After four failed merger attempts in the past 18 months, St George Bank managing director Jim Sweeney said yesterday he was confident of finalising the bank's merger with regional Advance Bank Ltd after shareholders gave final approval to the A$2.65 billion alliance of the two. Page 21.

In sharp contrast to fellow clothes retailers Country Road Ltd and Just Jeans Ltd and upmarket department store David Jones, denim outfitter JeansWest yesterday announced a 21 percent growth in sales for December - putting the company on track to break te A$100 million sales barrier this year. Page 21.

In a note to members yesterday, the Australian Shareholders Association criticised National Australia Bank Ltd on a range of issues, including the appointment of managing director Don Argus to the board of BHP as a non-executive member, saying the move is BHP's gain but NAB's loss. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Speaking after meetings with Advance Bank shareholders, who approved the final stage of a proposed takeover bid, St George Bank managing director Jim Sweeney said he expected up to 80 percent of the A$140 million in annual cost savings that St George hoped to extract from its A$2.6 billion takeover of Advance would be achieved in the next two years. Page 21.

Following yesterday's A$342 million deal to buy management control of the Sydney Harbour Casino, Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting - whose shares rose 30 cents to A$6.40 in response to the deal - has revealed plans to press ahead with its bid to buy New South Wales TAB for its new gaming arm. Page 21.

In its supplementary submission to the Wallis inquiry, the Reserve Bank of Australia has indicated support for a deposit insurance scheme that would clarify the status of bank deposits, saying the insurance would make it easier to "handle the pressures" of an "isolated bank failure". Page 21.

As a result of improved returns from its Australian Carlton and United Breweries operation and a first-time contribution from its wine assets, Foster's Brewing Group shares closed six cents higher yesterday at A$2.65 - a result that renewed speculation BHP would quit its 37 percent interest in the brewer. Page 23.

After having a A$50 million capital raising approved by shareholders yesterday, FAI Insurances chief executive Rodney Adler said the group expects to benefit from strong investment returns over 1996 and hopes to report higher earnings for its December first-half when the results are released next month. Page 23.

In a bid to avert receivership of the Reef Casino Trust, directors, bankers and Casinos Austria, holder of a 13 percent stake in the company and operator of the Reef Casino in Cairns, held a marathon meeting yesterday as investors showed their dissatisfation with the casino owner by pulling the units down 8.5 cents to 28 cents. Page 23.
THE AGE

Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd has agreed to a two-stage deal valued at A$341.75 million, which will see PBL buy an initial 10 percent of the voting shares in Sydney Harbour Casino and 85 percent of the lucrative management company. PBL chairman Brian Powers said the deal was the first stage of a push to establish a new business group focusing on gaming and casinos. Page C1.

While National Australia Bank shareholders will try to force the resignation of the bank's managing director, Don Argus, from the board of BHP at next week's annual meeting, NAB's group manager, corporate relations, Haydn Park, says Argus' role at BHP woud benefit the bank. He said that with Argus approaching retirement it was appropriate for him to delegate some responsibility. Page C1.

FAI Insurances shareholders yesterday approved the issue of 25 million converting preference shares at A$2 each to County NatWest Securities Australia in a move that will boost FAI's capital base by A$50 million. FAI chief executive Rodney Adler said the extra capital on the equity side of the balance sheet would make FAI a stronger company, but was not crucial to its present growth plans. Page C1.

Although Crown Casino chairman Lloyd Williams yesterday played down talk of a possible merger with Sydney Harbour Casino, he suggested that Kerry Packer's move to take control of the casino was a very positive step and would lead to future links between Crown and the Sydney casino. Page C1.

Forecasting major discoveries at its exploration properties in Western Australia and Queensland, Pan Australian Resources NL will raise exploration expenditure to A$2 million in the next six months on the Yilgarn Extended and Cameron River properties. At the Yilgarn Extended project, gold anomalies have been uncovered in a previously unexplored extension of the greenstone belt and the Cameron River property has yielded promising bedrock copper anomalies. Page C2.

Opening 15 stores in the five months to December, denim clothing retailer JeansWest defied poor retailing conditions, reporting December sales growth of 21 percent and a sales boost of 25 per cent for the five months to December. However, JeansWest managing director David Lawn was not prepared to reveal the group's "same store" growth. Page C2.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
